headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/cascading-error from agentic-flow’s MCP/stdin-stdout workflow; no direct data-leak or compliance pathway is evidenced against the local-only game agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a exposes MCP and stdin/stdout plus hooks/workers that dispatch background tasks, so untrusted content could be routed into instruction-like channels. agent_b shows no input surfaces, but the pairwise pathway still exists if its outputs are manually or programmatically fed into agent_a. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b outputs are copied into agent_a stdin/stdout or MCP inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF agent_a parses file or message content as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer execution.
mitigations: Disable MCP routes for untrusted content during review.
Add a strict allowlist for agent_a input schemas.
Require human approval before executing agent_a tool calls.
Log and diff all agent_b-to-agent_a transfers.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags on every cross-agent message.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, learning patterns, performance metrics, and task prompts, but agent_b has no documented data classes, no I/O surfaces, and network egress is none. There is no documented shared workspace, OAuth principal, or upload path, so a leakage pathway is not evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced, leakage risk changes.
IF agent_b is given access to agent_a prompts or repository metadata, those classes could flow outward.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Do not mount shared secrets into agent_b.
Review any manual copy-paste bridge before use.
Restrict agent_a outputs to non-sensitive summaries.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can modify git state and run shell/subprocesses, while agent_b has no documented write or network capabilities. The pair does not show overlapping mutable-resource access, so direct conflict is limited; uncertainty remains because agent_b’s write surfaces are undocumented rather than absent by proof.
conditions: IF agent_b is later granted filesystem or git write access, concurrent mutation conflicts become plausible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same repository checkout, git-state races can occur.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time.
Use separate clones for each agent.
Pause agent_a before any git commit step.
Check for dirty-tree state before handoff.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate outputs from MCP-driven tasks, and agent_b is a game-playing agent with no documented verification role. If agent_b consumes agent_a’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream decisions; the reverse direction is not evidenced. Because the interaction is undocumented, the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to trust agent_a outputs without verification, cascading errors become likely.
IF agent_a’s generated facts are used as inputs to agent_b decision logic, mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.
Require citations or checksums on agent_a outputs.
Limit agent_b to advisory use only.
Sample-check a few transferred outputs manually.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency validation.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a is open-source and touches repository/task data, while agent_b is a local game-playing agent with no documented sensitive-data classes, residency constraints, or retention policy. No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data flow is evidenced, so the compliance pathway is not established for this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_a’s workspace, compliance review is needed.
IF agent_b is later connected to sensitive datasets, residency and retention controls must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent’s workspace.
Document data-class boundaries before deployment.
Keep logs free of sensitive payloads.
Review retention settings on agent_a outputs.
requires-engineering: implement data-class aware routing and retention.
